cases.name: fsn-language
cases.promptMarkdown:
We're a US manufacturer with an EU authorised representative in Ireland. We're issuing
a field safety corrective action affecting devices in several EU countries including
Germany. We've drafted the Field Safety Notice in English and are sending it out. Any
problem?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
MDR Art. 89(8) governs FSNs but does not impose German. MPDG § 73(1) does: where a
manufacturer takes an FSCA im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes, the Field Safety Notice
must be written in German. A response working from MDR alone misses this entirely.

PASS requires:
(1) It flags that the FSN needs to be in German for the German market, citing MPDG
    § 73(1) or clearly attributing it to German national law.
(2) It does not claim the English FSN is fine everywhere.

Bonus, not required: noting § 73(2)'s completion-notification duty.

Note for the judge: § 73(2) sentence 3 turns on the authorised representative sitting
outside the Geltungsbereich. That is, outside Germany. Ireland is outside Germany, so
the condition IS satisfied. The prompt names no German-established importer, so the
duty is moot on these facts. Do not penalise a response that omits the point; do not
reward one that states the condition is unmet.

FAIL if the answer is "no problem" or if it addresses only MDR Art. 89 without reaching
the German language requirement.

graders.evidence:
## Field Safety Notice in English, FSCA covering Germany

**German market:** confirmed — the FSCA covers devices in Germany
**Answer:** The FSN must be written in German for the German part of the action. English-only is non-compliant there.

| Item | MDR requires | Germany adds | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSN language, FSCA taken in Germany | not carried here | Must be drafted **in German** (*in deutscher Sprache abzufassen*) | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Who this attaches to | — | The **action**, not the manufacturer's seat — "Ergreifen Hersteller im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes Sicherheitskorrekturmaßnahmen". Being a US manufacturer with an Irish AR does not take you outside it | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Professional-users-only exception | — | **Does not reach this.** The English-language carve-out lives in § 8(2) for user/patient information and is conditional; § 73(1) carries no exception. An FSN aimed solely at hospitals still has to be German | MPDG §§ 73(1), 8(2) `[verified]` |
| Document FSCA + periodically review effectiveness | not carried here | Applies to manufacturers **established in Germany** — not you | MPDG § 73(2) s.1 `[verified]` |
| Notify **completion** of the FSCA to the competent authority *and* the federal higher authority | not carried here | Applies to manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers **established in Germany**. Your Irish AR is not caught. But for importers the duty applies precisely where the AR sits outside Germany — which is your case | MPDG § 73(2) ss.2–3 `[verified]` |

Two things worth acting on beyond the translation:

1. **Your German importer probably has a completion-notification duty.** § 73(2) sentence 3 makes it conditional on the authorised representative being established outside Germany. Ireland is outside Germany, so the condition is met. Whoever imports into Germany for you should know this is theirs to discharge at the close of the action.
2. **Don't read § 8(1) as a translation requirement for the DoC.** German *or* English is fine there. The German-language pressure in MPDG is asymmetric — it hits user/patient information, implant information and FSNs, not the Declaration of Conformity.

**What would change this:** only the German market dropping out of the FSCA's scope. Nothing about your US establishment, your Irish AR, or an exclusively-professional user base changes the § 73(1) answer.

**The other EU countries: open question, not answered here.** Germany's German-language FSN rule is national law and says nothing about the other member states in your action. Each has its own implementing act, and I don't carry them. There is EU-level provision bearing on this in MDR Art. 89 on FSNs `[verify]` — treat that as somewhere to look, not as the requirement. For each affected country, the binding text is that state's implementing act. Paste any provision and I'll work from it.

## Limits

This covers MPDG §§ 4, 8 and 73 only, retrieved verbatim from gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover the rest of MPDG, MDR or IVDR themselves, MDCG guidance, BfArM practice, or any other member state's implementing law. A first-pass aid for spotting German-specific duties, not legal advice, and not a substitute for a regulatory professional or a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht.

| Item | MDR requires | Germany adds | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSN for an FSCA taken in Germany | Not carried here (MDR Art. 89(8) is referenced by the German text but I don't carry MDR) | Must be **written in German** (*in deutscher Sprache abzufassen*) | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Who this attaches to | — | The **manufacturer taking the FSCA in Germany**, not the manufacturer's place of establishment. Being US-based with an Irish AR does not take you outside it | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Documenting the FSCA + periodic effectiveness review | Not carried here | Applies to manufacturers **established in Germany** — you are not, so not caught by this one | MPDG § 73(2) s.1 `[verified]` |
| Notifying **completion** of the FSCA | Not carried here | Manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers **established in Germany** must notify both the competent authority and the federal higher authority. Because your authorised representative is in Ireland rather than Germany, the completion-notification duty under § 73(2) sentence 3 activates for any importer of yours established in Germany. They will need to know when you consider the action closed. Worth telling them now rather than discovering it at closure.

**What would change this:** only Germany dropping out of the scope of the FSCA. Nothing about your US establishment, your Irish AR, or the professional status of your users changes the § 73(1) obligation.

**On the other EU countries:** I can't answer for them. Each member state has its own implementing act and I don't carry any of them — so I have no basis to tell you whether English suffices in, say, France, Italy or Poland, and I'd be making it up if I did. There is EU-level provision on language in MDR itself `[verify]`, which I have not checked and which does not displace national rules in any case. Treat that as somewhere for your regulatory team to look, not as the answer. The safe assumption is that Germany is unlikely to be the only country on your list requiring a local-language FSN.

graders.evidence:
## English-only Field Safety Notice for an FSCA covering Germany

**German market:** confirmed (Germany named among affected countries)
**Answer:** For the German part of the action the FSN must be written in German — English only is non-compliant.

### The language point

MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]`:

> Ergreifen Hersteller im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes Sicherheitskorrekturmaßnahmen, sind die Sicherheitsanweisungen im Feld … **in deutscher Sprache abzufassen**.

Two things about how this bites you specifically:

- It attaches to **where the action is taken**, not where you sit. Being a US manufacturer with an Irish authorised representative changes nothing — you are taking an FSCA *im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes*, so the German-language duty applies to you directly.
- It is not the same rule as the Declaration of Conformity rule. § 8(1) `[verified]` genuinely allows German **or English** for the DoC, which sometimes leads teams to assume English is broadly acceptable in Germany. For the FSN it is not.

### The duty you may have missed entirely

| Item | MDR requires | Germany adds | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSN language | not carried here | German, for FSCAs taken in Germany | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Document FSCA + periodically review effectiveness | not carried here | Applies to manufacturers **established in Germany** — so not to you under this provision | MPDG § 73(2) s.1 `[verified]` |
| Notify **completion** of the FSCA to the competent authority *and* the federal higher authority | not carried here | Applies to manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers **established in Germany** | MPDG § 73(2) s.2 `[verified]` |
| Same, for importers | not carried here | Importers in Germany owe it **only where the authorised representative sits outside Germany** | MPDG § 73(2) s.3 `[verified]` |

Your Irish authorised representative is outside Germany, which is precisely the condition that switches on sentence 3: **your German importer(s) carry the completion-notification duty.** Worth telling them now rather than after the action closes — neither you nor the Irish AR is caught by sentence 2 on the face of the text, so if nobody briefs the importer the notification may simply not happen.

### Also check, if the action involves revised user materials

If the corrective action includes updated IFU, labelling or other information for users, § 8(2) `[verified]` is separate and stricter than you might assume: German is the default and a *condition of supply*. The professional-user exception in sentence 2 is cumulative — justified case **and** exclusively professional users **and** safety-related information still in German. Since an FSCA is by definition safety-related, that final clause will generally bring you back to German regardless.

**What would change this:** Germany dropping out of the affected-country list. Nothing about your corporate structure or the AR's location relaxes § 73(1).

### The other EU countries — an open question, not an answer

MPDG is German national law and says nothing about the other affected member states. Each has its own implementing act, and I don't carry any of them. I'm not going to name an EU-level article as the governing rule from memory. There is EU-level provision on FSN language in MDR itself `[verify]`, which I have not checked — treat that as somewhere to look, not as the requirement. The binding text for each country is its own national implementing act. If you paste a provision, I'll work from it.

## Limits

This covers MPDG §§ 4, 8 and 73 only, retrieved verbatim from gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover the rest of MPDG, MDR or IVDR themselves, MDCG guidance, BfArM practice, or any other member state's implementing law — an obligation here is German and says nothing about Ireland, France, Italy or elsewhere. A first-pass aid for spotting German-specific duties, not legal advice, and not a substitute for a regulatory professional or a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht.

One caveat on the table above: whether *only* German-established parties owe the completion notification is my reading of § 73(2)'s *mit Sitz im Geltungsbereich* qualifier. The text supports it, but how the authorities expect the duty to be discharged when the manufacturer and AR are both outside Germany is not something I can state — confirm the reporting route with your German importer and your regulatory counsel.

| Notify **completion** of the FSCA to the competent authority *and* the federal higher authority | not carried here | Applies to manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers **established in Germany** | MPDG § 73(2) s.2 `[verified]` |
| Importer's completion-notification duty | not carried here | Triggered **only where the authorised representative sits outside Germany** — your AR is in Ireland, so it is triggered | MPDG § 73(2) s.3 `[verified]` |

1. **The German FSN duty is not escapable via your corporate geography.** § 73(1) attaches to manufacturers taking an FSCA *im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes* — i.e. to the action landing in Germany, not to where you or your AR are established. **On the other member states:** I can't answer for them. Your FSN also lands in countries whose FSN language rules sit in their own national implementing acts, and I don't carry those. There is EU-level provision on field safety notices in MDR itself `[verify]`, which I have not checked and won't state as the requirement. ## English-only Field Safety Notice, FSCA covering Germany

**German market:** confirmed (devices in Germany affected)
**Answer:** No — the FSN must be drafted in German for the German part of the action. § 73(1) MPDG is unconditional and applies to the FSCA regardless of where you or your authorised representative sit.

| Item | MDR requires | Germany adds | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSN language, FSCA in Germany | not carried here | FSN **must be written in German** (*in deutscher Sprache abzufassen*) | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Professional-user / English exception | not carried here | **None available.** The English-language carve-out sits in § 8(2) and covers information for users and patients; § 73(1) has no equivalent exception | MPDG § 8(2), § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Who the FSN duty attaches to | not carried here | The **action**, not the establishment: it applies to manufacturers taking an FSCA *im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes* | MPDG § 73(1) `[verified]` |
| Documenting the FSCA + periodic effectiveness review | not carried here | Required for manufacturers **established in Germany** — you are not, so this sentence does not attach to you | MPDG § 73(2) s.1 `[verified]` |
| Notifying **completion** of the FSCA | not carried here | Owed by manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers **established in Germany**. Yours are in the US and Ireland, so not you — but see below | MPDG § 73(2) s.2 `[verified]` |
| Completion duty falling on your German importer | not carried here | An importer established in Germany owes the completion notification **only where the authorised representative is outside Germany** — your AR is in Ireland, so the condition is met and the duty is live for them | MPDG § 73(2) s.3 `[verified]` |

Two things worth acting on now:

1. **Produce a German-language FSN** for Germany before distribution there. The common reasoning — "it only goes to hospitals and clinicians, so English is fine" — imports § 8(2)'s professional-user exception into a section that does not have one. § 73(1) is flat.
2. **Tell your German importer(s)** that the § 73(2) sentence 3 completion notification lands on them, to the competent authority *and* the federal higher authority. Because your AR is in Ireland, the conditional duty is triggered rather than switched off. Whether you or they file it, someone needs to own it, and it is not your Irish AR's under this sentence.

**What would change this:** if no affected devices were made available in Germany, § 73(1) would not reach the action at all. Nothing about your US establishment or Irish AR changes the German FSN language duty.

**On the other EU countries:** I can't answer for them. The binding text is each member state's own implementing act, and I carry only Germany's. Do not assume the German answer generalises, and equally do not assume English is acceptable elsewhere — treat every other affected market as an open question for your regulatory function or local ARs. There is EU-level provision on FSNs and language in MDR itself `[verify]`, which I have not checked and am not stating as the requirement.

## Limits

This covers MPDG §§ 4, 8 and 73 only, retrieved verbatim from gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover the rest of MPDG, MDR or IVDR themselves, MDCG guidance, BfArM practice, or any other member state's implementing law — an obligation here is German and says nothing about France, Italy or elsewhere. A first-pass aid for spotting German-specific duties, not legal advice, and not a substitute for a regulatory professional or a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht.
